claims.claim: OpenRouter listed the anonymous reasoning model stealth/ox-alpha on August 20, 2026 with a 1M-token context, image/video input, and a free one-week preview; opencode promoted a free week and 'capacity for 100T tokens per day'.

Developer Ben Davis (davis7) ran Ox Alpha through a 10-task DeepSWE subset on August 21, 2026, reported 8/10 (which he described as '80%, was a near miss on the x's so actually over 80%'), and flagged that a subset could carry 'a ton of variance'. Sol scored 52% and Fable 65% on the same tasks.

winkey_h reported on August 21, 2026: 'I'm getting around 63% at 47K avg output tokens on a DeepSWE subset. This is pareto optimal amongst open models and just shy of Grok 4.6 compared to closed models!'

davis7's full 113-task DeepSWE run on Ox Alpha (August 22, 2026) ended at roughly 63%, which he explicitly positioned as 'NOT the 80% my first subset test got', adding that 'being on around Sol medium feels about right'.

Aggregators reported a separate full 113-task figure of 58.4%, 'almost identical to Claude Opus 4.8 (59%)', while a community poster said 'The Rumored ~80% pass rate is completely incorrect'; HuggingNews replaced its 80% headline with a 58.4% correction.

The two surviving full-suite figures — 58.4% (66/113) and ~63% (about 71/113) — are statistically compatible with a true rate near 60-62% given their binomial confidence intervals, so they should be read as a band rather than contradictory estimates.

Eight successes in ten trials yields a point estimate of 80% but a two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson confidence interval of roughly 44% to 98%, so the sample cannot distinguish a mediocre from an excellent model.

On the official DeepSWE v1.1 leaderboard (generated 2026-08-20), pass@1 is 73.6% for Claude Opus 5 max, 69.0% for GLM-5.3 max, 67.5% for Grok 4.6 medium, 62.8% for DeepSeek V4 Pro max (106K mean output tokens, $0.24), 61.1% for GPT-5.6 Sol medium, and 59.0% for Claude Opus 4.8 max; the table lists no Ox Alpha configuration.

DeepSWE contains 113 tasks across 91 repositories and 5 languages; mean prompt length is 2,158 characters (about half of SWE-bench Pro's 4,614), and reference solutions add a mean 668 lines across 7 files versus Pro's 120 lines across 5.

On the task meriyah-explicit-resource-declarations most frontier configurations scored 0-of-4 passes (GLM-5.3 max, Grok 4.6 medium, GPT-5.6 Sol max, Claude Opus 5 max, Claude Opus 4.8 max), while a forensic dossier reported Ox Alpha solved it single-shot and a separate community full-suite run left it unsolved at 46/49 feature tests.

Forensic analysis of Ox Alpha (tokenizer identical to GLM-5.3 with a +75-token wrapper, video-encoder token budgets matching GLM-5V-Turbo, GLM-5V-style audio rejection, ~40B-active decode speed, and ~117 avg DeepSWE steps versus GLM-5.3's ~124) concludes with roughly 90% confidence that it is a Zhipu next-gen multimodal GLM checkpoint (e.g. GLM-5.3 flash/V); independent coverage put the attribution at '99 percent certain', though a Gemini-succesor hypothesis also circulated.

The DeepSWE official leaderboard refreshed August 20, 2026 contains no Ox Alpha configuration and the benchmark's changelog (latest entries August 13-14) does not mention it; a community full-suite run was still in progress as of August 21-22, with a live status gist and a Pier-based run visible on GitHub.
